title: The anchors the pipeline must reproduce, and the order of magnitude references
why_a_seed: SPEC.md section 5.5 fixes a set of published figures this pipeline has to reproduce, and SPEC.md section 8 puts anchors.json in data/seed next to events.json. Holding them here rather than as literals in a test means the site can print the same numbers the tests assert, from one file, with a source_url on every one of them. Nothing fetches this file.
checked_how: The printed values are transcribed from SPEC.md section 5.5, which prints them from the DGEC notes named against each one. Every measured_* field was recomputed from the committed caches by the script that wrote this file, so the file cannot claim a reproduction the data does not support. The two source URLs were requested with curl on 2026-09-13 and what came back is recorded in url_status.

series_entries.anchors: The DGEC anchors of SPEC.md section 5.5, under Licence Ouverte 2.0 like every other DGEC figure in this project.
series_entries.sp_global_reference: The S&P Global order of magnitude figures, which are quoted from two news articles under ordinary quotation and are NOT redistributable as a series.
series_entries.why_two: One file, two manifest entries, because the two blocks are under different terms and the manifest records terms per series. Splitting the file instead would have put two hand written anchor files in data/seed for no gain.

mbr_monthly_usd_bbl.what: The published gross refining margin on Brent, as printed in the weekly note of the following month. SPEC.md section 9 makes these a test and SPEC.md section 10 says Gate 2 must not proceed if one fails.
mbr_monthly_usd_bbl.tolerance: None. SPEC.md section 5.5 says to stop rather than adjust the parser, so the comparison is the cache value rounded to two decimals against the printed value, exactly.

brent_july_2026_usd_t.url_status: 404 on 2026-09-13. This is not rot and it is not a mistake in SPEC.md section 5.6: the ministry publishes one weekly note at a time and deletes the previous one when the next appears, recon 02 section 2.3. The note of 28 August 2026 was live when the spec was written and is gone now. Ten notes survive only because this project archived them, and they are in data/private/dgec_notes, which is gitignored. THIS IS WHY THE WEEKLY NOTE HAS TO BE COLLECTED THE WEEK IT IS PUBLISHED.

brent_cross_check.what: SPEC.md section 5.5: DGEC Brent, converted with DGEC's own factor, against the monthly mean of FRED DCOILBRENTEU, within 1.5 $/bbl in at least 95 percent of months, listing every outlier.
brent_cross_check.monthly_mean_rule: Arithmetic mean of the days the source actually published a price. Weekends do not appear in the source. A blank day is not an observation of a price, so it is excluded from the mean, never filled and never carried forward. A month with fewer than the declared minimum of published days is NaN rather than a thin mean, and the observation count travels with every monthly value so an outlier can be reported as 'this month failed on 17 days of data'.
brent_cross_check.outliers_note: Empty, and that is the measurement rather than an omission. Not one of the 140 months exceeds 1.5 $/bbl. The worst is 0.2649 $/bbl. Two independent parsers and one conversion factor agree, which is what makes this cross check worth running.

sp_global_reference.what: Physical assessments quoted from two dated S&P Global articles. SPEC.md section 5.1 calls them order of magnitude references and SPEC.md section 5.5 asks for the MBR to be put next to them in the Gate 1 report. Different method, so a gap is expected; a gap of a different order would be a bug.
sp_global_reference.not_a_benchmark: SPEC.md section 6.6 forbids tuning toward these. Nothing in this project is fitted to them, they are never charted as a series, and they are never extended.
sp_global_reference.licence_note: Individual figures quoted from two news articles with attribution and a link, which is ordinary quotation. The underlying assessments are S&P's and are NOT redistributable as a series.
sp_global_reference.url_status_note: Both article URLs return HTTP 403 to automated access, with a bot token user agent and with a browser user agent, checked on 2026-09-13. The pages open in a browser. The figures below are transcribed from SPEC.md sections 3, 4.4, 5.1 and 5.5, which quote the articles, and were NOT re read from the source in this session. That is recorded here rather than papered over.

this_study_reports.how: gas cost 0.21217 x 39.02 $/MMBtu = 8.279, fuel oil cost 0.21217 x (60.75 / 6.287) = 2.050, difference 6.23. Four committed sources, nothing tuned. SPEC.md section 4.4 asks for this to be reported next to the S&P figure whatever it comes out at.
